text:
Lucas Raymond is the one Red Wing whose numbers have held up through a four-game slide. He has 18 points in 19 games, ten on the power play, and Heavy.com noted he's bucked the losing trend. With Dylan Larkin suspended and waiting on a trade, he and Alex DeBrincat are the team's offense.

His finishing is a little under normal (10.7% against a typical 13), so the goals should tick up. Detroit takes 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, which is better than the team's results. His points over the last ten games sit right about where his chances say.

Evolving-Hockey had him 26th of 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, against top competition, and a net positive on penalties. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man. At 24, he's become the player Detroit's next era leans on. Our range: 66 to 91 points.
